subject: MAP: weekly performance checkpoint — latency/throughput & next tuning steps
messages:
-----Message 1-----
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Procurement <cloud-procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Mar 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: weekly performance checkpoint — latency/throughput & next tuning steps

Hi all,

Quick sync notes from today's MAP checkpoint focused on the performance benchmarks we ran over the weekend. Objective: confirm whether current tuning moves get us within Acme's P50/P95 latency SLOs at target QPS for production ramp.

Attached: acme_map_latency_report_v3.csv, acme_map_throughput_summary.pdf, MAP-action-items-20270307.xlsx

Summary (short):
- Baseline model: rwd-infer-v2 (quantized int8)
  - P50: 78 ms
  - P95: 430 ms
  - Max sustainable throughput @ 250ms p95: ~60 qps
- Candidate optimized path: rwd-infer-v2 + KV-prefix cache + dynamic batching (batch size cap 64)
  - P50: 70 ms
  - P95: 310 ms
  - Max sustainable throughput @ 250ms p95: ~95 qps
- Alternative model variant: rwd-infer-small (8-bit + reduced head size)
  - P50: 62 ms
  - P95: 360 ms
  - Max sustainable throughput @ 250ms p95: ~110 qps but with noted quality delta on long-context prompts

Notable observations:
- P95 improvements using prefix KV caching are largest for repeated prompt prefixes (expected for Acme's triage flows).
- Throughput numbers assume request size average ~320 tokens/session; if average tokens increase to 500+, expect a 12–18% throughput drop.

Decisions & asks:
1) Marcus to validate memory pressure on dedicated nodes when enabling prefix caching at production QPS (action: Marcus) — due Wed 3/9.
2) Neha to run two A/B eval sets comparing rwd-infer-v2+cache vs rwd-infer-small on Acme's critical prompt set and report quality deltas (action: Neha) — due Fri 3/11.
3) Dylan to prepare a canary rollout plan for the cached path with automatic fallback to baseline when p95 > 400ms (action: Dylan) — due Mon 3/14.
4) Soojin to produce cost delta estimate (per-1M tokens) across the three configs and put into MAP sheet (action: Soojin) — due Thu 3/10.

Jordan — can you confirm whether the 250ms p95 target is still the bar for customer-facing triage? Also flag whether any region/country-specific latency constraints apply.

I'll follow up with the detailed CSVs and the MAP sheet link. Call-out: we'll propose a short maintenance window for cache-priming during the first canary run to stabilize p95.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198

-----Message 2-----
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Mar 2027 10:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: weekly performance checkpoint — latency/throughput & next tuning steps

Thanks Kim — ran deeper memory profiling overnight and attached a truncated CSV showing GPU memory timeline and cache hit rates (see acme_map_latency_report_v3.csv).

Quick findings:
- Enabling prefix KV cache increases GPU memory footprint by ~12% at steady state (per-node) for 32-byte KV chunks. With our current node types that is within headroom for the dedicated pool but reduces burst capacity by ~8%.
- Cache hit rate at 60 qps baseline ~55%; with request clustering (simulated by Acme traffic trace) hit rate moves to ~72%.
- Observed an increase in tail latency if batching timeouts are set too high (>20ms) — we should cap batching latency budget to 15ms for triage flows.

Action: I will spin a focused job to test cache eviction thresholds (LRU window) and report by Wed 3/9 EOD.

-Marcus

-----Message 3-----
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <cloud-procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Mar 2027 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: weekly performance checkpoint — latency/throughput & next tuning steps

Thanks for the thorough summary.

Confirmation: 250ms p95 remains the target for the customer-facing triage endpoint. Two clarifications:
- We expect burst QPS during business hours up to 120 qps (10% margin over the baseline business case). Can you confirm the cached path keeps p95 under 250ms at sustained 120 qps? The throughput numbers in the summary looked promising but wanted explicit confirmation.
- For the A/B evals, please prioritize the 'long-CT' prompt set (avg tokens ~480) — that's what drives most customer complaints today.

Procurement: we'll need a short note on whether any of these changes alter cost commitments under the Dedicated contract.

Jordan

-----Message 4-----
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Mar 2027 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: weekly performance checkpoint — latency/throughput & next tuning steps

Jordan — per your request I prioritized the 'long-CT' prompt shard in the A/B plan. Initial synthetic runs show the cached path holds p95 ~330ms at 120 qps with avg token 480, but that's above the 250ms bar. However, if we combine cache + the rwd-infer-small variant we get to ~240–260ms depending on exact prompt mixes; that's within margin but risks a small quality regression on hallucination-sensitive prompts.

I will run quality diffs (ROUGE/factuality checks + reviewer spot-checks) and attach results by Fri. If the quality delta is small, recommended plan is:
- Canary 1: rwd-infer-small + cache to hit the 250ms p95.
- Canary 2: rwd-infer-v2 + optimized batching (15ms cap) to compare quality/ops complexity.

Neha

-----Message 5-----
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Mar 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: weekly performance checkpoint — latency/throughput & next tuning steps

Adding the canary rollback criteria and schedule to the MAP sheet (see MAP-action-items-20270307.xlsx). Key points:
- Canary window: 02:00–06:00 PT for initial priming; monitor p95, error rate, and user-facing throughput.
- Rollback triggers: sustained p95 > 400ms for 5 consecutive minutes OR error rate delta > 0.5% above baseline.
- Fallback: automatic route to baseline model; manual paging only if both fail.

I'll coordinate with Ops to reserve the window and schedule a short dry-run on Wed 3/9.

Dylan

--- End of thread ---
